correctness.rationale: Each state traversal must experience a distinct residue class of effective b-hits to synchronize a coprime cycle, forcing n-1 merge letters. Along a trajectory with at least n-1 such hits, each intervening walk from k to 0 costs at least min((n-k)alpha,k gamma). Positive costs rule out detours at equality. The explicit alternatives shrink the image one state each and attain the bound. Exhaustive subset shortest paths for n=2..9 and 162 tested price cases check length, cost, tie counts and noncoprime obstructions; these finite checks supplement the proof.

value.rationale: Reversible control of a standard cyclic merging automaton naturally models asymmetric direction costs. The result completely classifies weighted synchronization in a nontrivial infinite family, identifies a sharp control-policy phase boundary, and counts exactly 2^(n-2) cooptimal reset words on the boundary, beyond either one-way threshold or isolated finite tables.
